item.title: Effective Methods to List Functions in a Python Module
item.description:
“Effective Methods to List Functions in a Python Module”

Techniques for Function Discovery in Python Modules

Several built-in tools and standard library modules facilitate the inspection of Python code elements. The optimal approach often depends on whether you need to execute the module’s code, maintain definition order, or strictly avoid execution side effects.

1. Utilizing dir() for Basic Listing

The simplest, most immediate way to see what an imported module exposes is using the built-in dir() function. This returns a list of names (strings) representing attributes, functions, classes, and variables present in the module’s namespace.

item.title: Python Techniques for Retrieving Function and Method Names Programmatically
item.description:
“Python Techniques for Retrieving Function and Method Names Programmatically”

How can a Python developer reliably extract the string representation of a function’s or method’s name, either from within its execution scope or externally, leveraging built-in attributes, specialized modules, or advanced wrapper techniques? Different scenarios necessitate different approaches, ranging from accessing simple attributes to detailed stack inspection.

Accessing Function Names Directly

The most straightforward technique involves accessing special attributes directly on the function object.
